fields.sample_size: participatory action research in three villages of the Agincourt health and demographic surveillance site (Bushbuckridge, Mpumalanga; 120,000 people, 31 villages, 21,500 households): eight community workshops (2-3 hours, weekly, June-September 2017; 52 participants in the pilot stage including 32 from two villages that nominated another priority) and seven further workshops with 16 community stakeholders on lack of safe water; three multisectoral workshops (January-March 2018) with provincial and district Department of Health officials, other departments and NGOs; two district planning workshops (September-October 2018)
fields.effect_measure: qualitative participatory action research with group model building and rich pictures, combined with verbal autopsy data from the surveillance site; no inferential statistics
fields.effect_estimate: Lack of safe water was nominated by community participants as a health priority; verbal-autopsy analysis attributed about 34% of the deaths recorded in the surveillance site in 2014/15 to lack of clean water. In multisectoral workshops government actors validated the community and statistical evidence on causes, health and social impacts and possible actions (Table 2) and a local action plan was drawn up; the process produced joint ownership, buy-in and mutual trust instead of protest. The authors conclude that bringing stakeholders together pools knowledge and may narrow the evidence-practice gap, and that the next stage is implementing and learning from action; no change in access was measured. Context: around five million South Africans lack access to safe water despite legislative commitments to participatory water governance.

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a participatory action research process to engage multisectoral stakeholders on lack of safe water as a community-nominated health priority in rural Mpumalanga; read in full text 2026-10-04. Process and priority-setting outcomes only; no access outcome measured.
